queries.title: Is the Marcus inverted-region boundary the Goldschmidt tolerance-factor boundary?
queries.chemicalQuestion: Marcus divides the driving-force axis at x = lam: the normal region is x < lam and the inverted region is x > lam. Goldschmidt divides the tolerance factor at t = 1: the ideal cubic packing is t = 1, and the classic cubic band is [0.8, 1]. Is the Marcus boundary lam the Goldschmidt tolerance boundary 1, i.e. does the tolerance factor measure a Marcus driving force?
queries.chemicalRationale: Marcus boundary lam = x is an equality between an energy (the reorganization energy) and a driving force; Goldschmidt t is a dimensionless ratio of ionic radii. A relation would need a total map from (rA, rB, rO) to (lam, x) and a statement that the boundary values coincide for all perovskites. No delivered statement provides such a map; the only shared word is "boundary".

queries.title: Is the Sabatier near-optimal band the Goldschmidt tolerance band?
queries.chemicalQuestion: Sabatier's NearOptimal tol apexD dE := |dE - apexD| <= tol and Goldschmidt's GoldschmidtConforms (1 - delta) (1 + delta) rA rB rO are both symmetric acceptance bands around an ideal value. Is the Sabatier within-tolerance optimum the Goldschmidt tolerance band, i.e. is the catalytic descriptor dE the perovskite tolerance factor t?
queries.chemicalRationale: The band shapes coincide: a symmetric interval about an ideal value is an absolute-deviation bound. But the scalars are a binding energy (dE) and a dimensionless radius ratio (t). The legacy §10 row registers exactly this as a look-alike of shape with no edge; Goldschmidt's window equivalence is exact for every band, while Sabatier's sharp condition carries the product condition 0 < alphaA * alphaB. A relation would need a total map between the two scalars, which no statement supplies.
